From 1837 to 1881 the regiment marched passed the saluting base to a tune called The Old Queen's, which included part of the national anthem. In 1881 this tune was played when 1/Queen's paraded before Queen Victoria at a review at Aldershot. The queen asked whether special permission had been given for use of the national anthem, adding, unamused, that unless it had, the practice must cease. No authority could be found, and so for a short time the regiment made its feelings clear by passing the saluting base without music, earning the nickname 'The Silent Second.'

Source:

Holmes, Richard. "Flesh and Blood." Tommy: The British Soldier on the Western Front, 1914-1918. London: HarperCollins, 2004. 113. Print.

I listened to a broadcast about social responsibility, and ..I'm not sure, it seems sort of undefined..but then again I am a physicist and like things in 'black and white' e.g. tell me what to do and I will do it, but this wasn't evident in the discussion

So what do you think is an example of social responsibility and do you feel it?
What is Social Responsibility and do you show it?

I would say "making the lives of others around you better in every small way you can manage."

Whether that's picking up trash when you see it, offering encouragement or a compliment to someone in passing, spending time to help your community either by volunteering or donating. That's a good start. Once you're read to commit to more time and energy, I would say bumping up the volunteer hours or maybe getting involved in local organizations that align with your interests. Whether that's a church group, a book club, a fundraising group, or a service non-profit, the world needs more people who are willing to give back.

I just wish I had more time and energy to practice what I preach. While there are a few things I do here and there to help, for the most part when I'm done with work I just want to go home and play video games or watch movies. Sometimes it feels like a wasted effort to do even the little volunteering that I am... mostly because I don't get that same sense of accomplishment anymore. It just feels like work they don't pay you for as opposed to something worthwhile. But that's not THEIR fault... it's MINE. I need to rediscover my own motivations again.
Leave things better than you find them, absolutely.

To me, it means to discover how to have your heart open always, and if you do that then everything else will follow. It sounds like bullshit, but you can train yourself to feel things-- anything-- with your heart, and there is wisdom in how your heart "thinks." You can look at a tree or a bug or a store clerk or a cityscape or a job and try to feel what it is about. Besides that, just keep going on about your life-- observing, taking care of your body, doing your job, doing what you love; but the fact that you took the time to build that compass in, where you are able to feel that every single thing is a part of yourself, you will never get off base and you will always make the right choice. It's not even like a set of values or a thinking process, it's just an inbuilt instinct that humans have and we tend to lose along the way, or use it selectively. But you can exercise it like a muscle, and you can decide to be a person with a big heart. Don't get caught up in different details or quotas on how much "service" you should do. A lot of times those situations are manipulative anyways-- lots of people come out of certain volunteer or service organizations totally jaded because they found out slowly that it was a racket, when they entered into it desperately wanting to fight the good fight. Same goes for organized religion and groups that try to intervene in things; a lot of times they can do good things but sometimes it's unclear whether it's best to "stay out of it." So just go on living your life but grow your heart, it will be a million times more valuable than anything else. Since you're a physicist, it will probably prevent you from doing the shady kind of shit that people do in the increasingly corporatized science world these days. You will "first do no harm" unlike many doctors or engineers or scientists who learned that phrase but can't feel in their heart of hearts whether what they're doing is wrong. If they wonder if it's wrong, they end up rationalizing it away or using some thought process to carry on with it. But your heart can't get confused like that and doesn't harbor contradictions. Always trust it and always put it first.
